name: read
description: Read a text file as `anchor│content` rows: a 4-character anchor (letters only, case-sensitive), `│`, then the line. Target edits by anchor, never by content or line number. `offset` takes a 1-indexed line number or a served anchor; with an anchor, `limit` counts lines from that anchor row onward — no line-number math. Page long files with `offset` and `limit`; when output says truncated, continue from the hinted `offset`. A stale anchor is refused with the current rows and fresh anchors. Images attach visually; binary, directory, and UTF-16/UTF-32 text are rejected; an empty file returns one empty row you can replace to seed content.
promptSnippet: Read a file; each line returned as anchor│content
promptGuidelines: Remember to use the hashline tools for every file read and edit: `read`, `replace`, `replace_match`, `insert`, `copy`, `move`, or `undo_last_change`.
`read`: call again after an edit when you need anchors you lack — post-edit diff `+`/` ` rows and served `anchor│content` rows already carry fresh anchors for the changed range.
`read`: `replace_match` needs both boundary lines served; copy `match` from a served row or read the lines first.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number (1-indexed) or a served anchor to start reading from

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read from offset; counted from the anchor row when `offset` is an anchor

name: replace
description:
Replace a range of lines (or a single line) in a text file by anchor. Deleting every line empties the file, and the result names the empty-line anchor, so a follow-up `replace` can seed content without a `read`.

To change only part of a line without retyping the rest, use `replace_match` instead; it preserves every character the request does not name.
promptSnippet: Replace lines by anchor: bare anchors in `remove_from`/`remove_to`, the exact replacement text in `text`
promptGuidelines: `replace`: same-message calls must target disjoint ranges.
`replace`: a pure deletion (`text: ""`) is the cheap way to clear a large range: it verifies only the first and last line against the served record and removes the interior as it currently stands.
`replace`: for a single line, use the same anchor for `remove_from` and `remove_to`.

`replace`/`replace_match`/`insert`/`copy`/`move`: same-file calls in one message commit as one batch. If you already know all the edits and their anchors, send them together instead of one turn at a time; an edit that needs anchors from a previous result waits for the next turn. Earlier calls reply `In batch N (queued)`, the last shows the combined diff, and one undo reverts all. A request-invalid call (anchors, shape, or `match`) fails alone; a failure while the batch runs aborts it.
`replace`/`replace_match`/`insert`/`copy`/`move`: anchors resolve the file; `path` is optional but must match anchor ownership when passed.

`replace`/`replace_match`/`insert`/`copy`/`move`/`undo_last_change`: in the post-edit diff, `-anchor│` rows are dead anchors; `+anchor│` and ` anchor│` rows carry live anchors for the next edit. Rows the diff does not show keep their anchors, so a follow-up edit on them needs no re-read.

`replace`/`replace_match`/`insert`: `text` is written exactly as received; escapes are decoded once when the call is parsed, and the tool never decodes again — `\uXXXX` is the character, `\\uXXXX` the literal text.

remove_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST line to remove.

remove_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST line to remove.

text.description: The exact text to write in place of the removed range. "" deletes the range. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line.

name: replace_match
description:
Replace part of a line — or the same fragment on several lines of a range — without retyping the rest. `match` is the exact text to find inside the anchored range, and `replacement` replaces every occurrence; the text around each match is left untouched. Send only the fragment that changes — never text that `replacement` leaves unchanged — and narrow `replace_from`/`replace_to` when only one occurrence should change. `match` only needs to be unique inside the anchored range, not file-wide. For a whole-line rewrite, use `replace` with the same anchors.

The two boundary anchors must still match what was last shown; lines strictly inside the range are searched as they are on disk.
promptSnippet: Replace part of a line or range by anchor: every `match` occurrence inside the range becomes `replacement`; the rest of each line stays untouched
promptGuidelines: `replace_match`: `match` is only the fragment that changes — never text that `replacement` leaves unchanged; every occurrence inside the range is replaced, so narrow the anchors when only some lines should change.

`replace_match`: the anchors bound the range searched, and `match`/`replacement` must each stay within one line — a trailing line break is the line's terminator, an interior one belongs to `replace`, and a lone break cannot be a `match`.
`replace_match`: when the change covers the whole line, use `replace` with the same anchor and the exact text.

replace_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST line of the range searched.

replace_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST line of the range searched; same as `replace_from` for a single line.

match.description: The exact text to find inside the selected lines, copied from the served row: only the fragment that changes, never text that `replacement` leaves unchanged. It must stay within one line and hold text: a single trailing line break is accepted as the line's own terminator, a line break anywhere else is refused, and a value that is only a line break leaves nothing to find and is refused. Every occurrence inside the range is replaced; the text around each match is left untouched.

replacement.description: The exact replacement for every matched occurrence within the range. "" deletes the matches. It must stay within one line: a single trailing line break is accepted and dropped (a value that is only a line break counts as ""), and a line break anywhere else is refused. The rest of each line is kept byte-for-byte.

name: insert
description: Insert text next to an existing line without removing anything. The anchor line stays in place, and `anchor` is a bare 4-character anchor from any served `anchor│content` row.
promptSnippet: Insert a text block after or before an anchor line: the anchor line stays; `text` is the exact text without anchor prefixes
promptGuidelines: `insert`: a missing or extra `+anchor│` blank row at either block edge in the diff is the classic insert slip.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the line to insert next to.

text.description: The exact text to insert; an empty string inserts one blank line. A trailing line break sets the newline of the last line written instead of adding a blank line; a lone newline writes one blank line. Never include the anchor line.

name: copy
description:
Duplicate a range of lines at another anchor. The source rows and anchors stay live; the copied lines get fresh anchors in the destination's post-edit diff and keep their source line endings.

A copy duplicates the content its source anchors were served from, so a same-message edit to the source file does not change what is copied.
promptSnippet: Copy lines to another position by anchor: `source_from`/`source_to` mark the range, `anchor` and `direction` the destination
promptGuidelines: `copy`: the same anchor in `source_from` and `source_to` copies one line; copied lines get fresh anchors in the post-edit diff and the source rows keep theirs.

`copy`/`move`: only the first and last marker rows and the destination line need anchors — grep the markers, the body is copied; to append to the end of a file, anchor that file's last line with `direction: "after"`.

`copy`/`move`: within one file the insertion point must fall before the source range's first line or after its last; anchoring the block's last line with `direction: "after"` (or its first line with `direction: "before"`) targets the gap right beside the block.
`copy`/`move`: `source_from` and `source_to` may live in a different file than `anchor`; an empty destination file is seeded with the copied or moved lines.
`move`: a batched cross-file move does not display the source file's diff; its removal commits with the batch, and the source file needs a read for fresh anchors.

source_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST source line to copy.

source_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST source line to copy.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the destination line; the block lands before or after it and it may live in another file.

direction.description: "after" places the block below the anchor line, "before" above it

name: move
description:
Relocate a range of lines to another anchor. Within one file the destination must sit outside the source range; moving a range onto itself reports `No changes made` and leaves the anchors alone. Rows between the source and the destination keep their content but may be re-anchored, so read that span again if you plan to edit it.

A cross-file move commits on its own when its source file also has batched edits in the message.
promptSnippet: Move lines to another position by anchor: `source_from`/`source_to` mark the range, `anchor` and `direction` the destination
promptGuidelines: `move`: moving a range to where it already sits reports `No changes made` and leaves the anchors alone.

`copy`/`move`: only the first and last marker rows and the destination line need anchors — grep the markers, the body is copied; to append to the end of a file, anchor that file's last line with `direction: "after"`.

`copy`/`move`: within one file the insertion point must fall before the source range's first line or after its last; anchoring the block's last line with `direction: "after"` (or its first line with `direction: "before"`) targets the gap right beside the block.
`copy`/`move`: `source_from` and `source_to` may live in a different file than `anchor`; an empty destination file is seeded with the copied or moved lines.
`move`: a batched cross-file move does not display the source file's diff; its removal commits with the batch, and the source file needs a read for fresh anchors.

source_from.description: 4-char anchor of the FIRST source line to copy.

source_to.description: 4-char anchor of the LAST source line to copy.

anchor.description: 4-char anchor of the destination line; the block lands before or after it and it may live in another file.

direction.description: "after" places the block below the anchor line, "before" above it

name: grep
description: Search text files with ripgrep. Hits come back as `lineNumber:│ anchor│content` rows and context lines as `lineNumber-│ anchor│content`, editable with replace, insert, copy, or move without a new read. A row returned by `grep` is already a served row, so you do not need to `read` the file to edit that line. The `=== path ===` header and line numbers locate the match. Patterns use ripgrep's Rust regex syntax (no backreferences or look-around) through a linear-time engine. Searches respect `.gitignore`, always skip `.git`, and skip binary and image files silently. A match over 500 bytes is shown as a `...` fragment around the hit, but its anchor still covers the whole line. When output is cut by the match limit, raise `limit`; when cut by rows or bytes, refine `pattern` or narrow `path`.
promptSnippet: Search with `lineNumber:│ anchor│content` hits (`lineNumber-│` for context) usable directly for `replace`/`insert`; use `literal`/`glob`/`context`
promptGuidelines: `grep`: set `literal: true` when the pattern contains regex metacharacters.
`grep`: `N:│` rows are matches and `N-│` rows are context;

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob; `*` crosses directories, e.g. `*.ts`. A leading `/` is ignored; relative to the search root or cwd.

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal text instead of regex

context.description: Lines of context before and after each match

limit.description: Maximum number of matched lines to return (default 100)

name: undo_last_change
description: Undo the last replace, replace_match, insert, copy, or move on a file, restoring the previous content, BOM, and line endings. If the file changed since that edit, the undo is refused and the file is left untouched; a file deleted since the edit is restored.
promptSnippet: Revert a file's most recent edit (single level)
promptGuidelines: `undo_last_change`: history is one slot per file, not a stack; a second undo returns `E_UNDO_NONE`.
`undo_last_change`: a `write` clears the history, so undo before any other edit or write; the undo diff's `+anchor│` rows are the restored lines.

`undo_last_change`: a cross-file `move` records one undo entry per file; undo both the source and the destination to revert the whole move, because undoing one side alone leaves the moved lines duplicated or missing.

path.description: Path to the file to undo
